newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Polish official seeks HK and Chinese investments.
newsitem.headline: Polish official seeks HK and Chinese investments.

text.p: Poland's Finance Minister Grzegorz Kolodko on Thurday urged Hong Kong businesses to invest in his country and help boost its exports.

"We've come here...to work out the possibilities of our export expansion to the Chinese market, Hong Kong, as well as to take advantage of the Hong Kong ability to trade, to get better access to Southeast Asian markets," Kolodko told a news conference at the end of his visit.
"Now I would like to enhance, to encourage inflow of the foreign-backed investment from Hong Kong and also from China," he said.

Poland was an emerging market with a working market economy and democracy and adequate skilled labour, he said. It could be a window to the European Union, which it aims to join this century, and to the Commonwealth of Independent States, he said.
Kolodko earlier paid a five-day visit to China, where he met Premier Li Peng, Vice Premier Li Lanqing and central bank governor Dai Xianglong.
Poland had decided to provide its export credit bank with US$360 million for Polish firms to boost exports to China, he said.
In Hong Kong, Kolodko met Financial Secretary Donald Tsang and local businessmen.
